routes.description: Establish that contingent reality calls for an explanation outside the totality of contingent things and that an automatically actual foundation is a better stopping point than brute contingency.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its explanatory principle legitimately applies to contingent reality as a whole, excludes a contingent explanans from completing the explanation, and supports a noncontingent foundation without requiring an indefensible account of necessity.

motionBridge.description: Show that the explanatory facts about contingent reality provide rational support for moving to an automatically actual or necessary foundation.

centralBridges.description: Specify and defend the principle that contingent things have an explanation and that their collective explanation cannot be one of the contingent things explained.
Justify extending ordinary explanatory and abductive reasoning to reality's foundational structure rather than exempting the totality from inquiry.
Explain why automatic actuality or noncontingency removes the distinctive explanatory demand generated by actuality that could have failed.
Provide a coherent route from explanatory fundamentality to an appropriate kind of necessity, including the relation between logical necessity and a concrete foundation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish relevant strengths of necessity so the foundational conclusion does not depend on epistemic certainty or an unnecessarily strong modal formulation.
Account for why apparent conceivability of a foundationless or godless world need not establish genuine metaphysical possibility.

routes.description: Establish that explanatory reasoning within contingent reality does not warrant a necessary foundation, because an ultimate brute or independent foundation may remain contingent and necessity adds no decisive explanation.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if global explanatory demands remain unsupported or if fundamentality, independence, and bruteness can be separated from modal necessity, leaving a contingent universe or other brute foundation as a live endpoint.

motionBridge.description: Show that the move from contingent reality or an unexplained foundation to a necessary or automatically actual foundation is not warranted.

centralBridges.description: Require justification for applying causal and explanatory intuitions formed within reality to spacetime, total reality, or its ultimate boundary.
Show why labeling a foundation necessary does not explain its actuality and may reverse or circularize the proposed explanatory direction.
Separate explanatory independence and absence of a further explanation from existence in every possible world.
Require a bridge from necessary logical or abstract truths to the necessary existence of a concrete, causally capable foundation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Establish whether comparable bruteness can be assigned to the universe or another contingent foundation without additional explanatory cost.
Test appeals to hidden contradiction and conceivability by clarifying when undiscovered identities or inferential consequences determine genuine contradiction.

sections.title: The explanatory principle and its application to total contingent reality
sections.rationale: This issue governs whether contingent reality generates an explanatory burden and whether the explanation must lie outside the collection of contingent things rather than terminate within it.

sections.title: Global explanatory inference versus a brute foundation
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether explanatory practices legitimately extend to ultimate reality and whether a brute universe or other foundation remains an adequate alternative endpoint.

sections.title: The explanatory role of automatic actuality and necessity
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether noncontingency answers the relevant demand for explanation or merely redescribes an unexplained foundation while introducing circularity about supremacy and necessity.

sections.title: Fundamentality, independence, and modal necessity
sections.rationale: This issue addresses the key transition from being ultimate, independent, or without further explanation to being unable not to exist across the relevant range of possibilities.

sections.title: Logic, conceivability, and a concrete necessary foundation
sections.rationale: This issue covers whether necessary logical structure supports a concrete foundation and whether conceivability, hidden contradictions, or abstract-truth commitments establish or undermine that connection.
